domain: Runs a battle presentation, copies motion-child state, performs a palette fade, cleans up actors, and dispatches the selected ability result through the battle-event queue.
notes: 2026-08-27: two structural, non-forced levers cut the gap from 624/306 to 600/290. (1) dispatch-shape: the AbilityInfo->kind dispatch was a `switch(kind){case 1: case 2: case 4:}`, which routed gcc296 lowered as a 3-way binary-search compare tree (test 2 first, then branch high/low). The reference instead uses a plain ascending if/else-if chain (kind==1, else (u8)kind==2, else (u8)kind==4) with no binary search. Rewriting the switch as that if/else-if chain matched the reference's compare order and alone took the candidate from 624 to 616 bytes (306 to 302 differing halfwords). (2) typed work record: `struct PresentationWork` was previously an opaque `u8 bytes[84]` accessed everywhere through `FIELD(base,type,offset)` (`*(type*)((u8*)base+offset)`). For the scalar/array fields (offset 0, 4, 8, the offset-20 loop count, the offset-36 s16 table, the offset-52 u8 values) that pointer-cast form was apparently treated by routed gcc296 as a distinct hoistable pointer value: it computed `&work+20` once into a dedicated register (sl) and reused that cached pointer for both the loop guard and the do-while tail check of the two `count`-bounded loops, instead of folding the constant +20 into each load's immediate offset the way the reference does (`ldr r3,[r5,#20]` recomputed fresh, base+immediate, no cached sub-pointer). Replacing those FIELD accesses with true struct-member accesses (work.field_00/04/08, work.count, work.table[i], work.values[i*4+j]) stopped that hoist: the frame shrank from the candidate's 92 bytes to 88 (now bytewise matching the reference's `sub sp, #88`), and size dropped 616 to 604 (302 to 300 diffs). The runtime-indexed second-loop access (`FIELD(&work, s16, saved_offset)`, offset not known at compile time) was deliberately left as macro-based pointer arithmetic since it already matched the reference exactly. (3) loop-local index: scoping the first loop's index into its own block-local `s32 i1` (previously it shared the function-wide `s32 i` used by three unrelated loops) shaved a further 4 bytes, 604 to 600 (300 to 290 diffs) by improving cross-loop register coalescing. The identical scoping trick applied to the second (saved_offset) loop was tested and reverted: byte-identical output, it only reshuffled which physical registers (r6 vs r7) carried the same roles.

Remaining, confirmed NOT reachable through legitimate C restructuring: inside the first loop routed gcc296 strength-reduces BOTH linear accesses keyed off the loop index -- work.table[i] (stride 2) and work.values[i*4+j] (stride 4) -- into persistent per-iteration accumulator registers. The reference binary only strength-reduces the stride-4 (values) access; the stride-2 (table) address is recomputed fresh every iteration via `lsls r3,r7,#1; adds r3,#36` from the work-base register (r5), never cached. That extra cached accumulator is exactly the difference between the candidate needing 7 simultaneously live registers during the first loop (input, selection, object, work-base, loop counter, table-accumulator, byte-accumulator) and the reference needing 6 (no table-accumulator) -- with only 6 non-fp callee-saved slots available (r5,r6,r7,r8,r9,sl), the 7th forces the candidate to additionally save/restore fp, which the reference never touches. That single extra register is the root of essentially all of the remaining diff: it costs ~8 bytes of prologue push/mov and ~8 of epilogue pop/mov directly, and it reassigns which physical register (r8 vs r9 vs sl vs fp) carries each of input/selection/object/work for the rest of the function body, so almost every later instruction differs only in register number, not in shape. This was tested directly and could not be changed short of forcing register assignment (disallowed): switching work.table[i] between struct-array-indexing and raw FIELD-macro pointer arithmetic produced byte-for-byte identical output either way, and giving the loop a dedicated index variable (vs. the earlier fix that did help for other reasons) did not by itself suppress the accumulator. The strength reduction appears to be an intrinsic, all-or-nothing decision of gcc296's induction-variable pass for a loop with two same-index linear array accesses, not a decision exposed to source-level control.

Secondary, minor residual: in the second dispatch arm ((u8)kind==2), the reference re-derives the truncated byte via `lsls r3,r2,#24; lsrs r3,r3,#24` immediately before the compare, even though r2 already holds a zero-extended byte from the preceding `ldrb`, making that mask provably redundant. Routed gcc296's value-range analysis elides the same redundant mask in the candidate. This costs a handful of halfwords and was not chased further, since the register-count gap above dominates the remaining diff by more than an order of magnitude.

Explicit register-qualified carriers remain byte-neutral: this was re-tested for `register s32 object` (the whole-function-lived object id, not just the pointer carriers noted previously) with zero effect on the emitted bytes.

Old agbcc produces 572 bytes with 308 differing halfwords (against the original 624/306 candidate baseline; not retested against this draft). The register mismatch that remains is still pervasive across 5 physical registers (r5 matches; r6/r7/r8/r9/sl/fp all carry different logical variables than the reference at various points) and is judged very unlikely to close further without either a different gcc296 IV-optimization decision than routed gcc296 makes for this loop shape, or forcing register assignment, both out of scope per CONTRIBUTING.md.
Retained assembly remains authoritative and this draft claims zero bytes. No inline assembly, fixed-register variable, compiler barrier, invented compiler flag, or copied instruction bytes were used.
